slides.title: Chandraghanta, the bell-shaped moon
slides.sub: The third form of Durga, worshipped on Tritiya

slides.title: The bride, ready to protect
slides.body: After her marriage, the Goddess adorns her forehead with a half-moon shaped like a temple bell. Her form is martial and alert, and the sound of her bell is said to drive away negative forces.

slides.title: Lion, ten arms, a bell-moon
slides.body: She rides a lion or tiger, carries weapons in her ten arms and wears the bell-shaped half-moon on her forehead. She combines grace with readiness to protect.

slides.text:
पिण्डजप्रवरारूढा चण्डकोपास्त्रकैर्युता ।
प्रसादं तनुते मह्यं चन्द्रघण्टेति विश्रुता ॥
slides.translit: Pindaja pravararudha chandakopastrakairyuta, prasadam tanute mahyam chandraghanteti vishruta
slides.meaning: She who rides the finest of beasts and bears fierce weapons, renowned as Chandraghanta: may she extend her grace to me.

slides.title: Chandi Path: 700 verses, 13 chapters
slides.sub: What the priest reads during Durga Puja

slides.title: Reading as worship
slides.body: Chandi Path is the reading aloud, as worship, of the Devi Mahatmya, also called the Durga Saptashati or the Chandi. It is part of the Markandeya Purana: 700 verses in 13 chapters.

slides.title: Three stories, 13 chapters
items: Ch 5: the Ya Devi Sarvabhuteshu hymn
Ch 7: Kali slays Chanda and Munda

slides.title: The companion hymns
items: After: Devi Suktam and the three Rahasyas
The exact order varies by tradition

slides.title: Who reads it, and when
slides.body: In Bengal it is part of the priest's duties on each main day, often read by a second priest alongside the worship. In old family pujas it may be read in the thakur dalan each morning, Saptami to Navami.

slides.title: Can't read Sanskrit? Listen.
slides.body: Many traditions value shravana, attentive listening, as worship. Experienced readers finish all 13 chapters in about two to three hours; some spread it over days. Your family priest's guidance comes first.

slides.line: Mahalaya dawn: many Bengali homes hear the Chandi on the radio

slides.title: Read slowly. Or simply listen.
slides.ask: Send it to your family's Chandi reader

caption.en:
Chandi Path at Durga Puja 2026: what Kolkata's priests are reading 📿

The Devi Mahatmya, or Durga Saptashati: 700 Sanskrit verses in 13 chapters from the Markandeya Purana. Chapter 1 is Madhu and Kaitabha, 2 to 4 are Mahishasura, 5 to 13 are Shumbha and Nishumbha.

In Bengal the priest reads it on each main day of the puja, often with the Devi Kavacham, Argala Stotram and Kilakam before the chapters. The exact sequence varies by tradition.

Can't read Sanskrit? Many traditions count attentive listening as worship, and many Bengali homes hear the Chandi on the radio at Mahalaya dawn.

slides.sub: Pujor jama from Shashthi to Dashami

slides.title: Five days, five outfits
items: Shashthi: first new outfit, cotton or handloom
Saptami: comfortable festive wear for walking
Ashtami morning: garad, korial or silk sari
Ashtami evening: the dressiest, for many
Navami: something special for the last night
Dashami: lal-paar sada for sindoor khela

slides.title: Names you'll hear
items: Tant: crisp handloom cotton for daytime
Dhakai jamdani: almost sheer, light, dressy
Baluchari: Bishnupur silk, heavy and formal
Garad and korial: white silk, red border
Tussar: textured silk for day or evening

slides.title: Dhuti-panjabi and beyond
slides.body: Dhuti-panjabi is the traditional pick for anjali, family pujas and Dashami. For pandal hopping, a panjabi or kurta with pyjama or jeans, in cotton, khadi or silk blends. Silk or tussar for evenings.

slides.title: Broken-in, not brand new
slides.body: You may walk many kilometres in a night on crowded roads. Wear broken-in shoes or sandals with soft soles and good grip. Slip-ons help where shoes come off. Carry new footwear in a bag for one or two stops.

slides.title: Fabrics that breathe
slides.body: Handloom cotton, khadi, linen and light jamdani by day; heavy silks for the evening. Carry a light scarf for sun or a sudden shower, and safety pins to keep pleats in place in crowds and on escalators.

slides.line: Dashami: a lal-paar sada sari, and clothes that can take some colour

caption.en:
What to wear for Durga Puja in Kolkata, day by day from Shashthi to Dashami 🥻

Pujor jama means new puja clothes, and many of us plan a different outfit for each day. Cotton tant or handloom by day. Jamdani, Baluchari or silk in the evening. A garad or korial for Ashtami anjali, and a lal-paar sada sari for sindoor khela.

There's no strict dress code, though. Kolkata's warm and humid in October and you may walk many kilometres in a night, so breathable fabric and broken-in shoes matter as much as style.

slides.title: How a Durga idol is made at Kumartuli
slides.sub: Bamboo, straw, river clay and, last of all, the eyes

slides.title: The frame and the straw
slides.body: Work starts months ahead. A kathamo of bamboo and planks carries the weight; in an ekchala image the goddess, her four children, the lion and Mahishasura share one frame. Tied straw sets the posture.

slides.title: Clay from the Hooghly
slides.body: The straw is covered in clay from the Hooghly, the local stretch of the Ganga, mixed with rice husk or chopped straw so it doesn't crack. Once dry, a smoother coat of finer clay goes on.

slides.title: Punya mati
slides.body: By tradition the clay includes soil from several places, among them a handful from the doorstep of a sex worker's home. Many image-makers still follow it, though not all, and its meaning is debated.

slides.line: Faces usually come from moulds, many of them family heirlooms

slides.title: Chokkhu daan, the eyes
slides.body: The last brushstrokes are the eyes, traditionally on or around Mahalaya, often by the senior artisan. Until then the image is unfinished. Then come the sari, jute hair and sholar or daker saaj.

slides.title: Walk the lanes
slides.body: The four weeks before the puja are the most rewarding. Take the Metro to Shobhabazar Sutanuti and walk west to the river. Go in the morning, wear closed shoes, ask before photographing anyone, don't touch the images.

caption.en:
Kumartuli, Kolkata: how a Durga idol is made, from straw to chokkhu daan 🎨

Bamboo and planks for the frame. Rice straw for the bodies. Then layers of clay from the Hooghly. Faces are usually made in moulds, many of them family heirlooms, and the eyes, chokkhu daan, are traditionally painted around Mahalaya.

Kumartuli is the potters' quarter of north Kolkata, on the river between Sovabazar and Bagbazar. If you can, walk its lanes in the weeks before the puja; by Shashthi most images have left for their pandals.
